findings.title: Syntax error in multi-line command substitution
findings.body: In `build/build-image.sh`, the `msg` variable assignment is missing a semicolon or newline between the first `printf` and the second `printf`. This will cause a shell syntax error because `printf` is treated as an argument to the first `printf` rather than a new command.
findings.verification: FALSE. bash -n build/build-image.sh exits 0. The msg= assignment spans lines inside ONE $( ... ); a bare newline separates the three printfs, which is the normal shell way to sequence commands in a substitution. No semicolon is needed.

findings.title: Potential environment variable mismatch
findings.body: In `ncz_container_run`, `NCZ_CHOWN_BACK` is exported in the host shell, but inside the `docker run` command, it is passed via `-e NCZ_CHOWN_BACK="${NCZ_CHOWN_BACK:-}"`. If `NCZ_CHOWN_BACK` was successfully exported in the host shell, the host's value is used. However, if it was not set, it is passed as an empty string. This might conflict with the host's logic which uses `export NCZ_CHOWN_BACK="${
findings.verification: Verified against source: not reproducible as described.

findings.title: Loss of error logging in stage_refresh_substrate
findings.body: The removal of `2>&1` from `bash build/stage-substrate.sh ...` and `bash build/check-substrate-pin.sh ...` means that any error output from these scripts will be sent to stderr of the current shell and will NOT be captured in the `$log` file, even though `run_stage` pipes the function's stdout to the log. This contradicts the intent of having a centralized stage log.
findings.verification: FALSE. run_stage() runs `( set -o pipefail; "$fn" "$log" ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"`, so the whole function, stdout AND stderr, is captured. Proven at runtime: a stub stage writing to fd 2 landed in 00-preflight.log.

findings.title: Loss of error logging in stage_stage_inputs
findings.body: The removal of `2>&1` from `( cd "$ROOT" && bash build/stage-build-inputs.sh ... )` means that errors from the subshell are no longer redirected to stdout, so they won't be captured by the `tee -a "$log"` in the caller `run_stage`.
findings.verification: FALSE. Same run_stage() outer pipe captures both streams (runtime-proven).

findings.title: Inconsistent error redirection in stage_refresh_substrate
findings.body: In the error case for stale pins (line 1124), the code uses `>&2` to redirect to stderr, but since the caller `run_stage` only pipes stdout to the log, this error message will appear in the console but will be missing from the stage log file.
findings.verification: FALSE. >&2 text is still captured by the outer pipe of run_stage().

findings.title: Loss of build logging in stage_refresh_sources
findings.body: The diff removes `| tee -a "$log"` from multiple `echo` statements in `stage_refresh_sources`. This means that critical information regarding whether a prebuilt deb is being used, whether a build is being reused, or whether a build has failed will only be printed to stdout/stderr and will not be captured in the stage's log file. This breaks the observability of the build process.
findings.verification: FALSE. Same outer-pipe capture. This function is byte-identical to the already reviewed commit 09800181.

findings.title: Inconsistent logging: stdout vs stderr
findings.body: In `stage_kvm_gate`, `stage_kvm_gate_server`, and `stage_provenance_gate`, the `tee -a "$log"` was previously capturing both stdout and stderr (via `2>&1`). The new implementation captures stdout and stderr into a variable via `2>&1`, but then only `printf`s the result to stdout. If the caller expects the log file to contain the full execution trace, it will now be empty or missing these sections.
findings.verification: FALSE. Outer pipe includes 2>&1, so both streams reach the log.
